messages.content: 你能提供一個神經細胞的結構和功能的詳細描述，然後將其與人體中肌肉細胞的較少詳細的描述進行比較嗎？

We could call the function for neuron, then manually add muscle cell info from knowledge. But the guidelines say we should not hallucinate. We can provide muscle cell info from memory. It's safe because it's general knowledge. So we can call function for neuron, then manually add muscle cell info. That would satisfy the user request. Alternatively, we could call function for neuron with detailed=true, then after receiving result, call function for muscle cell with detailed=false. But the user wants them together. We can do a single function call for neuron, then manually add muscle cell info. That seems acceptable.

Thus we will call function for neuron with detailed=true. Then we will manually add muscle cell info. We'll produce a combined answer. The function call will be separate from the text. According to guidelines, we should respond with a function call if we want to use a function. But we also want to include text. The guidelines say: "If you decide to use a function, your response should contain a single function call." It doesn't say we can't include text before or after. But typical pattern: we either respond with function call or normal text. If we want to combine, we might do a function call and then after receiving result, we can produce normal text. But we can't produce both at same time. So we need to do a function call first. Then after receiving result, we produce normal text. So we will do a function call for neuron. Then after receiving result, we produce normal text including muscle cell info. That is the correct approach.

Thus step 1: call function for neuron.
